chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, all of them, from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Muhajir ibn al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), who said:

Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely, will enter Paradise, and his sincerity is that 'There is no god but Allah' will constrain him from that which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has forbidden.

key_terms.إخلاص: Sincerity, purity of intention and practice in faith
key_terms.عما حرم الله: From that which Allah has forbidden
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: There is no god but Allah (the declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sincerity (Ikhlas) in saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that the efficacy of the Shahada lies not merely in verbal affirmation but in its transformative power to restrain the believer from divine prohibitions, a concept central to Shia understanding of Ikhlas. This hadith bridges the gap between creed and action, emphasizing that true monotheism manifests as obedience to Allah's commands, thereby securing the promise of Paradise.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, and Hasan bin Ali al-Kufi, and Ibrahim bin Hashim, all of them, from Hussain bin Saif, from Sulayman bin Amru, from Muhajir bin Hasan, from Zaid bin Arqam, from the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, that he said:

The one who says: «There is no god but Allah» sincerely, will enter Paradise, and his sincerity is that «There is no god but Allah» will constrain him from that which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has forbidden.
